assets.reason: The 2026-08-03 raw observations remain replayable, but Tool Catalog, Skill loading, and conversation Tool exposure changed afterwards; current resume metrics require a selective paired retest.

The recorded execution results remain historical evidence, but the model Profile, Agent orchestration, and SQL investigation contracts evolved after the run; current execution accuracy requires a bounded selective retest.
The deterministic QueryGuard fixture remains reusable for its frozen safety rules; it is separate from model-generated SQL execution accuracy.
The deterministic PostgreSQL FTS observations remain a valid scoped historical baseline and can be recomputed locally; they do not represent the later Vector, RRF, Rerank, or answer-generation path.
Parent expansion, rewrite, compression, and rerank observations remain historical evidence, but current Profiles and retrieval contracts require local recomputation followed by selective retesting.
The three-case decision fixture remains reusable, but current Agent orchestration and Evidence Gate behavior must be selectively retested before claiming current quality or Token gains.
The reviewed Judge input fixture remains reusable for schema and deterministic citation-contract validation; Provider-backed Judge output is auxiliary and is not a current M4 metric.

The seeded and recorded observations remain usable for contract replay, but the Conversation Runner, citation repair, context governance, and model Profiles changed; current answer-quality claims require selective recorded-run retesting.
The sample fixture remains useful for evaluator contract tests but does not represent the current production Agent path or a resume-quality benchmark.

The recorded set contains one early SQL-focused pair from before the current Conversation-driven diagnosis, Evidence Gate, knowledge, and context-governance paths; retain it for history but do not use it as the M4 comprehensive baseline.

The deterministic reviewed fixture validates the Early Exit switch, quality gate, per-case issue reporting, and zero-Provider Ledger replay; Provider-backed latency and quality claims still require an explicitly budgeted selective run.
The frozen throughput corpus and historical report remain useful, but current parser and worker changes require local validation and a bounded selective rerun before current throughput claims.
The parser evaluator remains current as an entry point, but its external corpus inputs and parser implementations must be revalidated before current quality claims.
The frozen public layout corpus remains reusable for its documented routing-only boundary and must not be presented as OCR, VLM, or end-to-end RAG quality.
Historical OCR pairs remain scoped evidence, but cloud model versions and provider behavior are time-sensitive; only explicitly budgeted cases may be retested.
The local VLM fixture remains reusable for schema validation, while Provider quality and latency are time-sensitive and require explicit bounded retesting.
The frozen local PPTX element corpus remains reusable for deterministic element extraction and routing checks within its documented scope.
The table evaluator remains valid, but current parser and recovery changes require corpus validation before reusing aggregate quality claims.
The historical GitHub Code Search incomplete-result observations remain useful, but the external service and current MCP adapter are time-sensitive and require selective retesting.

The fixture and historical report remain useful, but Current Summary coordination and the controlled long-conversation sequence changed after earlier pilot runs; local replay and the bounded current acceptance sequence must be rerun before reusing metrics.

All 120 pairs are human-reviewed and the current text-embedding-v4 profile passed the 98 percent Precision gate on Calibration and Holdout. The Holdout accepted only one hit, so the result remains a conservative fixed-set release gate rather than a production-wide accuracy claim.

The five-question fixed traffic replay measured current pgvector lookup and configured-provider full-chain latency under a 21-call hard budget; it is an acceptance replay, not a production traffic percentile.

PostgreSQL and Redis Stack were evaluated behind the same semantic-cache contract, dataset, threshold, candidate limit, conflict filter, and fixed traffic boundary. Redis Stack remains optional because its faster isolated lookup did not improve the full-chain P95 enough to justify another required service.
